newsitem.title: USA: Hilton Hotels sees Q1 shr $0.24 to $0.26.
newsitem.headline: Hilton Hotels sees Q1 shr $0.24 to $0.26.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp expects first quarter net income of about $65 million, or $0.24 to $0.26 a share, up from the year ago figure of about $37 million, or $0.19 a share.
Analysts had expected Hilton to report earnings of $0.23 a share with a range of $0.21 to $0.28, according to First Call.

Marc Grossman, Hilton senior vice president of corporate affairs, told Reuters the earnings growth resulted chiefly from a few factors. He cited strong winnings in baccarat play at the Las Vegas Hilton, revenue growth at its upscale hotels and contributions from recently acquired hotels and casinos.
Baccarat is a card game that is preferred by many high-rolling gamblers at the Las Vegas Hilton, and the hotel's wins or losses at the game can cause earnings to fluctuate.

First quarter earnings also benefitted from acquisitions of Bally Entertainment's hotel/casinos in Las Vegas, Atlantic City and Mississippi, as well as its purchase of six upscale hotels in major U.S. cities from The Prudential Insurance Co.
Hilton's strategy through 1996 and into 1997 is to be a leader in the gambling industry as well as an acquiror of upscale hotels.
Grossman added Hilton's upscale hotels continued to show revenue per average room (REVPAR) growth in the low double digits, which also contributed to the first quarter's higher earnings.
Hilton expects to report first quarter earnings on April 23.
